Send us your name, location, your chosen edition, and 3-5 sentences explaining why. Our favourite responses will receive a copy of former Long Wave editor Jason Okundaye’s book Revolutionary Acts: Love and Brotherhood in Black Gay Britain – part of the Guardian Bbookshop’s Black History Month collection. articles.title: How to turn excess custard into a fruity treat – recipe
articles.summary: A fool is absurdly simple – just fruit stirred through custard or yoghurt with. maybe a bit of cream – and you can then add whatever bits and bobs you fancy from the fridge.
body: Fool is one of my go-to desserts for two reasons: first, its pure simplicity – it’s little more than custard or yoghurt mixed with whipped cream and pureed fruit – and, second, its adaptability to the seasons. Gooseberry, rhubarb and strawberry are traditionally the most foolish fruits, but just about any fruit goes. British blackberries are still available and apples are in their prime right now, so I’ve gone for those, but use whatever you’ve got in store.

I usually make fool with yoghurt, not least because it’s much less work than making custard from scratch, but I’ve got lots of leftover custard from this week’s Food Filter taste test, so I’m going for a custard base here. I’m always looking for ways to use up small amounts of bits and pieces in the fridge, such as the end of a pot of custard or yoghurt, then add a few other ingredients to elevate remnants into regalia.
points: A fool is absurdly simple – just fruit stirred through custard or yoghurt with. maybe a bit of cream – and you can then add whatever bits and bobs you fancy from the fridge.

articles.title: Hold the lime! Could eating citrus zest and peel really be bad for your health?
articles.summary: Food safety campaigners have long been concerned about pesticide residues on lemons, limes and oranges – and now a social media post about it has gone viral. How safe is it to eat lemon cake or drink a G&T with ice and a slice?
body: D o you sprinkle citrus zest on to your cooking or drink hot water with a slice of lemon? According to an Instagram post that went viral last week, you shouldn’t. “Select citrus fruits at Lidl now come with a ‘Peel unfit for consumption’ warning,” posts @wholefoodwarrior. She photographs some of the supermarket’s labels, which list the post-harvest chemicals used to conserve the fruit: azoxystrobin and fludioxonil (limes) and imazalil, 2-phenylphenol, thiabendazole, pyrimethanil and fludioxonil (easy peelers), plus E903 in the peel’s wax coating (both).
The 10,500 comments on the post are largely appalled. So what are these substances? And how worried should consumers be?

So while the warning labels may be new, the use of these pesticides certainly isn’t. “Citrus fruit regularly tops our ‘ Dirty Dozen ’ list of produce found to be high in multiple pesticide residues,” says Compson. “This can include highly hazardous pesticides banned from use in the UK and Europe due to their toxic impact on people and the environment.” This year, grapefruit topped the list, with limes in third place. Over the past five years, soft citrus, oranges and lemons have always featured in the top seven.

articles.title: The 38 Best Restaurants in Barcelona, According to a Local Food Guide
articles.summary: From Barcelona’s towering churches and bustling avenues to the sun-drenched beaches and idyllic plazas, it’s obvious why this city captures visitors’ hearts. You can also eat incredibly well here, and often for not very much money — though Barcelona loves a tasting menu and the World’s 50 Best…
body: Start with some classic tapas and paella (both great but neither entirely Catalan) and be sure to seek out local gems like bittersweet vermouth, seasonal seafood, and homestyle Catalan cuisine. But after writing and revising this list for nearly a decade, I have to insist you don’t overlook the city’s burgeoning global cuisines; save room for Calabrese paninis, Northeast Asian sharing plates with natural wines, towering fried chicken sandwiches, South Indian fish stews, and nose-to-tail yakitori.

We update this list quarterly to make sure it reflects the ever-changing Barcelona dining scene. Our write-ups include insider tips from our experienced writers and editors, as well as a rough range of pricing for each destination — ranging from $ for quick, inexpensive meals with dishes largely under $10 (or the equivalent in euros), to $$$$ for places where entrees exceed $30.

New to the map in October 2026: Lluritu, a Mediterranean marisquería with three locations across the city; a parallel universe of Catalan culinary history in a former water bottling plant at Franca; and the trendy modern Catalan cuisine of Manda Huevos.

articles.title: 12 Best Anti-Aging Serums For Smoother, Plumper Skin at Any Age
articles.summary: In choosing the best anti-aging serums, experts recommend incorporating not only SPF, but ingredients like retinol, peptides, and vitamin C. Shop our favorites here.
body: I really should get into a more predictable skin-care routine. But at 46, and with so many of the best anti-aging serums to choose from, I feel like a kid in a candy store where all the sweets magically stimulate collagen production. But with other dermatologist-adored classics and buzzy new launches to choose from, it’s hard to narrow down the best treatments for my particular skin concerns. Do I use peptides to target my fine lines? Or is it time to get serious about exosomes? Is hyaluronic acid still the best thing for hydration? Or is PDRN the ingredient my skin has been missing? With so much information to consume, it’s easy to succumb to analysis paralysis.
points: In choosing the best anti-aging serums, experts recommend incorporating not only SPF, but ingredients like retinol, peptides, and vitamin C.

articles.title: Heels Are So Back—But Do You Remember How to Wear Them?
articles.summary: With the power pumps of decades past now transformed by whimsical proportions, charming prints, and eccentric embellishments, training yourself to wear them properly has become the latest form of self-care.
body: Taking in the spring runway shows in New York in September, I couldn’t help but notice how many of my fashion friends and peers had transformed themselves over the summer: They were now tan, yes, and thinner—but also, suddenly, taller.

Surveying the high heels across the front row at Fforme, I was reminded of Raye’s anthemic call for women to step into their Jimmy Choos and stand in their power (“Click-click-click-clack symphony, I need that”).

“I think there’s a real return to sexy, feminine dressing right now, and heels are naturally part of that,” Brigitte Chartrand, Net-a-Porter’s chief buying and merchandising officer, told me after the show from atop her own pair of black-and-mint-green Chanel pumps.

The revival, however, is a new proposition for a generation with no muscle memory for heels. Trying on a pair of Coach slingbacks with a three-inch block heel, I faced my bedroom mirror. My posture had collapsed, and I was pitched forward like a ski jumper. Before I could feel high and mighty, I would need to master standing up straight.

articles.title: You Can Preorder XReal's First Wired XR Glasses
articles.summary: The VR headset may be becoming a thing of the past. At Google's Android Developer Summit this morning, XReal officially debuted XReal Aura XR glasses, smart glasses with full XR capability.
body: Customers in the United States, Canada, Japan, and South Korea can order XReal Aura on XReal's site starting today, and they're expected to begin shipping in mid-November. The limited-time launch price is $1,099 for the 12GB + 256GB configuration and $1,299 for the 16GB + 512GB configuration, $180 and $200 less, respectively, than XReal announced earlier this month.
If the claim of mixed reality in a pair of sunglasses seems dubious, I tried them out a few months ago, and they are exactly that.

Instead of an enclosed headset, XReal Aura projects digital content on transparent lenses so you can be present in the real world while also in the digital world. Unlike "traditional" virtual reality headsets, the Aura's batteries and main compute are in a wired puck/controller you can slip into your pocket. That keeps the weight down and makes them comfortable enough to wear for longer periods. Because it's built on Android XR, users will have access to millions of 2D and 3D Android apps right out of the box.
If you want to go beyond Android, you can plug a USB-C-compatible computer or gaming console into Aura, and use that device in the same virtual space as native Android XR apps.

articles.title: The 12 Best Handbags for Travel, From Roomy Totes to Structured Satchels
articles.summary: Heading on a trip? Pick up one of the best handbags for travel to accompany you, from roomy totes to elegant top-handles you can also use at your destination.
body: Regardless if you’re on team carry-on or checked luggage, a travel handbag is the essential that unifies the masses. The requirements are universal: these carryalls must be spacious enough to store essentials like laptops, airplane toiletries, passports, and any miscellaneous gadgets—but they should also complement your personal style. And, preferably, be versatile enough that they can be carried throughout your trip.

The travel handbag I use religiously checks off all these boxes. Demellier’s Stockholm tote entered my life earlier this year and we’ve been inseparable ever since. Aside from the fact that it’s gorgeous—crafted in chocolate in a bowling-bag silhouette—the functionality means I’ve been relying on it for every single one of my trips, from long-haul journeys to quick overnight getaways. The roomy interior has a dedicated laptop compartment, multiple pockets for organization, and even a hidden magnetic slip pocket on the interior (this is where I conceal my passport and it’s changed my life).

articles.title: A Look Back at Julia Roberts’s Best Hair Moments of All Time
articles.summary: The Oscar-winning actor is celebrated for her million-dollar smile, but over the years, she’s proved that her shape-shifting mane will always make a statement.
body: There’s hair, and then there’s iconic, era-defining Julia Roberts hair, a mane worthy of awards. The Oscar-winning actor’s million-dollar smile may be her aesthetic signature, but since the start of her career, Roberts’s hair has proved a close second—in all of its many iterations.

Blame it on “The Rachel” effect, but the mid-’90s saw Roberts beginning to embrace face-framing, shoulder-sweeping styles that ran the gamut, from a swoopy fringed lob to a sleek layered chocolate bob—yes, Roberts was Team Bob before much of the famed 2026 bob community even had their first haircut. Among her most iconic moments was the wispy, twisted knot (and fuzzy underarms ) she wore for the premiere of Notting Hill in 1997, embodying the era’s easy, never overthought beauty attitude.

Speaking directly to her host of hair transformations, Roberts previously told Vogue: “I think there’s something in me that’s always [let] people feel they’re comfortable, or they see something familiar. If someone sees me in a grocery store and they say, ‘Why did you cut your hair like that?’ it’s not because they’re trying to be rude. It’s because they feel they know me, that I sit behind them in church every Sunday.”
points: The Oscar-winning actor is celebrated for her million-dollar smile, but over the years, she’s proved that her shape-shifting mane will always make a statement.

articles.title: Foraging for Purple Sea Urchins Along California's Sonoma Coast
articles.summary: Writer and chef Joseph Ogilvy heads to the intertidal zone in search of the umami-rich delicacy that's mowing down California's kelp forests.
body: This article is part of a series of stories about hunting, fishing, and foraging experiences across North America. Joseph Ogilvy is the author of Tin Can Coast, published in July 2026.

It’s low tide, not long after dawn, and we’re about to disturb the tide pools of a small Sonoma cove in a hunt for sea urchin. Our group of would-be foragers are in Sea Ranch, a couple hours north of San Francisco, on the tough end of the California coast, where fog-pressed hills tumble into the Pacific. The tide pools of Pebble Beach are covered in shaggy mats and bundles of kelp, and the spots that aren’t blanketed in seaweed are a carnival of alien creatures: sea stars, anemones, crabs, abalone, a muddled parade of luminous colors and implausible body shapes.
points: Writer and chef Joseph Ogilvy heads to the intertidal zone in search of the umami-rich delicacy that's mowing down California's kelp forests.
